# Draft:Solomon King (and The Chosen)

----
Jeff Laine (born 16 July, 1951), known professionally as Solomon King, is an American singer, songwriter, guitarist, and actor.
Born and raised in Detroit’s Eight Mile section, he has performed and/or recorded the Blues, Rock and Americana with The Chosen the umbrella name of his supporting band of “gypsies” which has included: Paul Butterfield, Billy Cox and Buddy Miles (of Jimi Hendrix), ace Motown producer Sylvester Rivers, Ray Parker Jr (Ghostbusters), vocalist Vanetta Fields (Pink Floyd, Steely Dan, Bob Seeger), teen prodigy Johann Frank (Englebert Humperdinck), and, also members of the famous Carradine performing clan including Robert “Bobby” Carradine and Calista Carradine at the Coachella Valley Music Show.
He’s performed all around the world from Arizona’s The Stock Exchange (Bisbee), to Hawaii with the Honolulu All Stars, and across America's heartland to Europe, Israel and Australia. Jeff Laine previously had a record deal with his Hollywood Underground band in 1988 with Apache Records.
But in 2008, he assumed the stage name of Solomon King. Then in 2009, King released his first album Under The Sun, produced by Motown legend Sylvester Rivers who brought in the ace rhythm section of Motown hitmakers.
The Rivers-produced Under The Sun was a Grammy entrant nominee in the “Best Contemporary Blues Album” category. Two of the songs from Solomon King's debut album, “Jack Me Up” and “Frankie and Johnnie,” were featured on the soundtrack in the first season of HBO’s acclaimed vampire series “True Blood.”
King’s other albums after Under the Sun, include: Medicine (2011) with producer Marvin Etzioni, founder of Lone Justice; Train (2014); and, blues rock LP, Against the Current (2017)
Now with remarkable synchronicity, this former Motown resident, who had recorded with those legendary Motown players, has recently performed at the Sycuan Casino Resort in El Cajon, and also did seven sold-out shows at the Rubicon Theater Company in Ventura, California. He performed as lead guitarist in “Forever Motown," a full on “Hitsville U.S.A.” show, featuring seven singers and a rousing five-piece band, bringing back some of the greatest music ever.
But Solomon King (and The Chosen) is also “remotely” recording a brand new album of original music for 2020, and is leaning on his rock blues background and "taking it to another level." Indeed, he makes reference to R&R pioneer Bo Diddley and the chain of responsibility he feels: “Bo’s classic, ‘Who Do You Love?’ revolves around one chord (A-flat). ‘Baby Does Me Good,’ my first song off Train came out of the over 200 live performances I did before the album—and there’s just one main chord to the song. Bo would do this—how do you take one chord and make it interesting for 25 minutes? That was my challenge. And, I continue to lean on that certain energy, that guys like Bo brought, and bring it to new music. Our job as performers and songwriters is to bring that long chain of special energy that goes way back and to reinterpret and express this energy through new music that resonates with a contemporary audience. Energy that celebrates joy and tears, makes you want to dance, and appreciate the gift of being alive, all the pains and joys of it.”
